notes: Intro: mid-market e-comm post-purchase platform focused on returns processing and shipping notifications.
Primary pain: high volume spikes during promotions/peak season causing chat latency and escalations to human agents.
Current stack: Zendesk + homegrown webhook layer; considering moving NLP/agent layer to Redwood for consistent streaming and tool calling.
Use-case detail: conversational agent to handle returns/shipping status, offer labels, create RMA, surface order info via tool calls to ERP/WMS.

Latency SLO: targeting p95 <= 300ms for agent responses (non-blocking streaming acceptable, final response budget 300-500ms), especially during peak loads (Black Friday windows 3-6x baseline traffic).
Throughput: typical daily concurrent sessions 150-400, peak events ~2500 concurrent for 4-12 hour windows.
Cost sensitivity: mid-market; willing to commit to Dedicated if unit economics beat hosted for peak periods; wants clear cost model for bursting.
Security: requires SSO/SAML for console, SOC2 + audit logging, ability to route some sensitive workflows to VPC Dedicated in future.
Model preferences: prefer smaller quantized models for cost-critical flows, fallback to higher-quality models for escalations; interested in Redwood's model catalog and quantization recommendations.
Quote from CTO: "We need predictable p95 during promotions — if it spikes our CS ops costs explode."
AE notes: Demo 2026-01-18 showed smooth streaming but we need synthetic load test with real tool-calls to ERP. POC scope agreed: 2 weeks Hosted POC + synthetic load test, chart p95 + error rates.

POC metrics: success criteria = p95 < 350ms under 2.5k concurrent synthetic sessions, <1% error rate on tool calls, stable KV cache hit rate >60%.
Procurement: procurement loop scheduled after POC; likely to evaluate Dedicated reserved capacity for holiday window if numbers align.
Next steps logged: schedule load-test script handoff, provide pricing scenarios for Dedicated + burst, set up SSO test account.
